feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the technical/digital blend is compelling. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and could be tightened to improve impact, reduce duplication, and sharpen results.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within one organization strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Good scope and specificity: examples like a 10,000+ page Drupal migration, 3.5M annual page views, and analytics stack modernization add substance.  
- Strong positioning for digital strategy roles: combines communications leadership, platform expertise, governance, analytics, and multimedia well.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” These sections overlap heavily and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond scale: include improvements in engagement, conversion, efficiency, adoption, or cost/time savings where possible.  
- Minor writing/style fixes: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience”; maintain consistent serial comma usage (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is slightly awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and foregrounding public-sector/advocacy relevance would make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with your senior positioning and sector relevance: digital strategy, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Replace broad terms like “programs” and “systems” with more concrete language such as “enterprise web platforms,” “editorial workflows,” and “cross-channel campaigns.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social, content, and multimedia operations for mission-driven and advocacy-focused organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, enterprise web modernization, editorial workflow design, and stakeholder coordination. Skilled at translating complex policy and technical topics into clear, accessible content that supports engagement, advocacy, and organizational goals.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Stakeholder coordination” also appears elsewhere; keep it here only if central to target roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value, senior-level capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, leadership-level language: “Digital transformation strategy,” “Editorial systems & governance,” “Web platform modernization,” “Analytics & performance reporting.”
- Reduce overlap with softer phrasing like “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination”; consider “Cross-functional leadership” only if you keep a people/leadership angle.
- Group related items for consistency and parallel structure; suggested version: Digital transformation strategy • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS modernization • Editorial systems & governance • Analytics & performance reporting • Workflow architecture & automation • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Standardize style: use either “and” or “&” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication” and “Policy & advocacy communication” repeat ideas already stated in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and is less compelling in a core competencies section.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the footer projects and prior NACo entries. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and the highest-value themes: enterprise web improvement, Drupal campaign delivery, and AI-enabled search.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading enterprise web improvement, campaign platform delivery, and content operations.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets; keep 4–5 max. Combine systems/workflows/analytics into one impact-oriented bullet and combine governance/usability/channel advice into another.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing efficiency gains, search engagement, reduced support tickets, or faster content turnaround.
- Use stronger action/result phrasing, e.g. “Built Drupal microsites and modular storytelling components that enabled reusable campaign launches and member resource distribution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects rail; keep one concise mention here and let the project section hold the detail.
- Drupal microsites/storytelling/toolkits also overlaps with “We Are Counties Microsite” in the footer.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and multi-channel communications operations.”
- Combine and tighten web impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add budget/team size, reporting improvements, production volume, or efficiency gains from governance and analytics systems.
- Rephrase weaker bullets to show change: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, bringing advocacy and event video production in-house” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to strengthen decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this item focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video/programming language also appears in older NACo roles; emphasize studio build-out and in-house capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item is too close to the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused, emphasize scope you directly owned, and add any concrete growth/volume metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy messaging and cross-team editorial execution.”
- Rewrite bullets to stress ownership and outcomes:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.
- Coordinated editorial calendars and content workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Standardized digital publishing processes to improve consistency, turnaround time and cross-team coordination.
- If available, add metrics such as newsletter open/click rates, video cadence/views, publishing volume, or workflow time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” overlaps with the Director role’s channel oversight.
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager entry and Recent Projects section.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around senior leadership value rather than generic capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, less repetitive wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy messaging
- Audience strategy, content planning & storytelling
- Consider reducing to 4 lines to improve scanability and avoid repeating “digital strategy/governance/multi-channel communications” already stated elsewhere.
- If space allows, make one line outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise content operations for high-volume, multi-publisher environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications leadership” substantially duplicate Core Competencies and the header.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also repeats language used in Core Competencies; “membership” would add useful specificity.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the platforms/technical strengths most supported by recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping or de-emphasizing WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages unless they are important for target roles; recent experience is overwhelmingly Drupal-centered.
- Replace “technical execution” jargon with clearer impact-oriented language such as “front-end implementation” or “platform delivery.”
- If space allows, add one proof point in adjacent experience bullets rather than here, e.g. 10,000+ page migration or AI search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep this section higher-level and save full tool inventory for the technical section.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies; avoid repeating all three verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:

- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. This topline item should emphasize strategic analytics leadership, not repeat software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive and leadership reporting • Dashboard development (GA4, Power BI, Looker Studio) • User behavior analysis (Microsoft Clarity) • Data analysis with BigQuery • SEO and performance optimization”
- Put higher-value, leadership-oriented skills first: KPI design, executive reporting, analytics strategy.
- Trim to 6–7 items max; group tools in parentheses instead of listing each separately.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie to impact in experience bullets instead of here (e.g., reporting that improved decision-making across a 10,000+ page site).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader digital strategy unless positioned as optimization/measurement.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and make it feel more senior than a generic production list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task-level to capability-level language: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “Studio buildout and operations.”

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize most relevant platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**; move **GitHub Pages** to a lower-priority item or drop it unless used recently/professionally.
- Consider adding proficiency framing: **Enterprise CMS platforms: Drupal (primary), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages**.
- If space allows, add brief context instead of just names: **Drupal site builds/migrations • WordPress publishing • SharePoint intranets • Power Pages**.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; “Web Platforms & CMS” is fine, but avoid repeating the same list elsewhere verbatim.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” Topline Skills entry almost exactly.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid over-listing it without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to **Front-End & Implementation Tools** to make the scope clearer and less repetitive.
- Replace broad/dated formatting with a tighter list: **HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- If accurate, add specificity that reflects recent impact, e.g. **custom front-end components, tag deployment, serverless scripts, CI/CD support** rather than only tool names.
- Consider dropping version numbers (**HTML5/CSS3**) unless other skills also use versioning; it dates the section without adding value.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** and **API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid reintroducing it here unless tied to a distinct tool or outcome.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/most relevant tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- Consider adding light functional grouping for scanability: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, replace one or two generic tools with higher-impact specifics (e.g., **approval workflows, intake systems, cross-team planning**) elsewhere in experience bullets rather than expanding this list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills, so avoid overemphasizing them here.
- Slack/Teams are low-signal unless collaboration tools are important to the target role.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platforms to include, but this item is currently just a vendor list and misses the scale/ownership implied by your recent NACo and consulting work. It should also avoid repeating “email” too broadly since multi-channel communications is already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses to show depth, e.g. **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation)** • **Higher Logic (member communications/newsletters)** • **Mailchimp (email campaigns)**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, place it first to reflect recency and strongest hands-on use.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with Work Experience bullets about leading email newsletters reaching tens of thousands; keep this item platform-focused, not outcome-focused.
- “Engagement” may feel vague alongside “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies; consider “Member Engagement” if that’s the real context.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content operations, and any concrete outputs or scale.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles as part of NACo’s first in-house digital team, helping formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: website refresh size/traffic, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, or production volume.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating seniority: “Produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- Consider a sharper version: “Promoted across two roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improve multi-channel publishing workflows, support a major website refresh, and produce recurring livestream and weekly video content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is repeated in later NACo roles; keep this version focused on initial team/process setup.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams.”
- Make the podcast achievement the centerpiece: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a more specific line such as “Produced digital and multimedia content to support policy communications and member engagement.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on innovation/research support plus the first-podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating digital leadership here since stronger, more recent leadership evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.
